function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability** | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • A single pane of glass that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards that surface latency, throughput, CPU/memory usage, network I/O, and cost per workload. | Unilever can see the health of its global supply‑chain, retail, and consumer‑engagement workloads in one place, eliminating the “cloud‑silos” problem. | | **AI‑Driven Root‑Cause Analysis** | • Machine‑learning models that correlate performance anomalies with underlying causes (e.g., a spike in CPU due to a new marketing campaign).
• Automated alerts that include suggested remediation steps. | Faster incident response means less downtime for e‑commerce sites and fewer disruptions to manufacturing pipelines. | | **Predictive Capacity Planning** | • Forecasts of future resource demand based on historical trends and upcoming events (e.g., holiday sales, product launches).
• Recommendations for right‑sizeing or scaling resources before they become bottlenecks. | Unilever can avoid over‑provisioning (cost savings) while ensuring capacity for peak demand periods. | | **Cost Optimization & Chargeback** | • AI models that identify waste (idle VMs, over‑provisioned storage) and recommend rightsizing or spot‑instance usage.
• Chargeback/Showback dashboards that tie spend to business units or product lines. | Enables Unilever’s finance teams to allocate budgets accurately and incentivize efficient use of cloud resources across departments. | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | • Declarative policies that enforce compliance, security, and cost limits automatically across all clouds.
• Auto‑remediation workflows that spin up or down resources based on policy violations. | Reduces manual toil for Unilever’s DevOps teams and ensures consistent governance across the enterprise. | **Key Differentiators vs Native Cloud Tools** | Feature | Turbonomics | Native Cloud Tool (GCP, AWS, Azure) | |---------|-------------|-------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud (multi‑cloud + hybrid) | Single‑cloud only | | **Unified Dashboard** | One UI for all clouds | Separate consoles per provider | | **AI/ML Models** | Proprietary models trained on multi‑cloud data; continuous learning across providers | Provider‑specific analytics; limited cross‑provider correlation | | **Cost Optimization** | Unified cost view, chargeback, and rightsizing recommendations across all clouds | Cost insights limited to the provider; no unified chargeback | | **Automation** | Policy‑driven auto‑remediation that spans clouds | Automation scripts or services limited to provider APIs | | **Data Aggregation** | Pulls telemetry from all clouds into a common data lake; normalizes metrics | Each provider stores metrics in its own format and location | | **Vendor Lock‑In** | Vendor‑agnostic; no dependency on a single cloud | Tied to the specific cloud’s ecosystem | **Bottom Line for Unilever** Turbonomics gives Unilever a *single, AI‑powered lens* that cuts through the complexity of managing workloads across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on‑prem environments. It turns disparate telemetry into actionable insights, automates remediation, and aligns cost with business value—something native cloud tools can’t do in a unified, cross‑cloud way.
